title: YES
html_source:
Yes begins and ends “Penelope,” a series of eight long, unpunctuated sentences. The formless stream resists categorisation. The non-style differentiates it from the rest of the chapters, facilitating the complex characterisation of Molly and indicating that we are to take her revelations as read. The chapter has contributed to feminist critical theories.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Molly thinks ‘yes’ scores of times throughout this chapter. Usually she uses the word to affirm something she is thinking. What is she affirming here? What is the antecedent to ‘Yes’?

We can usually understand what Molly is thinking once we identify the person involved. But there are several instances where short passages seem to just pop in out of the blue and defy interpretation with the context of the surrounding thought stream. See below for examples.
